routes.reason: Part II of the Tau Ceti ModularForms roadmap for noncongruence modular forms, the λ-function and the unbounded denominators theorem (60 items). The title reproduces that roadmap's atlas title 'Modular forms — Hecke theory, newforms, and L-functions' exactly, em dash included, the area automorphic is a galaxy id, and the brief is 573 words. Tau Ceti roadmaps are never re-planned, so a Part II is the right form, and nothing in the atlas plans noncongruence subgroups, the Wohlfahrt level or the integrality of Fourier coefficients on arbitrary finite-index subgroups. The λ-covering H/Γ(2) ≅ C∖{0,1} is claimed here because no layer plans it, and I found none.

Part II of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence for arithmetic algebraization and holonomy rank bounds (20 items). The title reproduces the parent's atlas title exactly, the area analytic is a galaxy id, and the brief is 341 words that name the theorems and their Mathlib inputs. DT.5 is 'Mahler functions, E/G-functions, algebraic independence and source-scoped functional-transcendence applications'; it has no algebraicity criterion of Borel–Pólya–Carlson–André–Bost type and no quantitative holonomy bound, so this is a new direction of the same roadmap rather than a stage of it.

Part II of the Tau Ceti ConformalMapping roadmap for the uniformization of punctured planes and value distribution on the disc (37 items). The title reproduces 'Conformal mapping and the geometric theory of holomorphic functions' exactly, the area analysis is a galaxy id, and the brief is 390 words. That roadmap stops at simply connected domains, and Mathlib's Nevanlinna theory is for functions meromorphic on C, so neither covers C∖μ_N or Nevanlinna theory on the disc; again a Part II because the parent is Tau Ceti work.

Source of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence DT.5 for Chudnovsky, Bombieri–André and Katz's local monodromy theorem, the G-function inputs that make the local monodromies quasi-unipotent in the proof of Theorem 7.3.3. DT.5 plans E- and G-functions with their differential equations, which is exactly where these belong.

Source of ModularCurvesPartII R14.4 for the Γ(N) form of Ihara's lemma, the amalgam presentation of the level-N subgroup of SL₂(Z[1/p]) and the congruence subgroup property. R14.4 is 'Ihara and level-change statements … and the proof using the relevant group-theoretic input', so the tree-of-SL₂(Q_p) inputs belong inside it.

Source of AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.2 for Shimura's bounded-denominators theorem. R15.2 is 'the q-expansion principle at all cusps …, its integral version and the finite-generation/base-change statements for spaces of forms', and Shimura's theorem is the companion integrality statement at every prime.

Source of ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7 for the universal-coefficient and Sylow reductions and the Künneth formula for mod-ℓ cohomology of products of profinite groups. D7 is described in the atlas as the sole generic owner of the extensions of upstream ProfiniteCohomology, including coefficient comparisons and continuous Hochschild–Serre, so these general inputs of §4.5 sit there.

Source of NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.0 for Lazard's H*(G, F_p) ≅ ∧*H¹(G, F_p) for p-powerful torsion-free pro-p groups. NE.0 builds completed group rings of p-adic Lie groups and takes its homological input from Lazard, and this is that input in the form §4.5 uses.

Source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 for H¹(SL₂(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 for p ≥ 3 except p = 5. G7 does plan the enormous-image conditions — its description defines an absolutely irreducible H as enormous when it has no nontrivial p-power quotient and H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0 — so the computation and its p = 5 exception belong there.

notes: Accept, no corrections needed. Both recorded hashes reproduce: the publisher's offprint (867026fb…) and arXiv v4 (9bffb129…). The offprint is an encrypted PDF, which is why a naive extraction of it yields nothing; I decrypted it with the standard security handler (RC4-128, R = 3) and read the published text directly, so the page numbers below are the journal's. Structure: 148 items (129 missing, 14 library, 5 planned), every missing item routed exactly once, no route takes a planned or library item, all six source stage ids exist, all planned layer ids exist, all three Part II parents exist and the proposed titles reproduce their atlas titles exactly (including the em dash in the Tau Ceti ModularForms title), all three areas are galaxy ids, and check_paper.py passes. The three proposed roadmap ids appear in no other extraction, so nothing is duplicated. Coverage: 124 numbered environments appear in the published text and every one of them is cited by an item (the five my checker flagged are artefacts of glued cross-references such as 'Theorem 2.0.1.1.1.7'). Locators: of 158 name-and-page checks 147 land on exactly the page given, and I read every one of the other eleven — each is a 'proof of X, p.N' locator where the statement sits on p.N−1, which I verified for Lemma 2.1.2 (p.638) and Lemma 4.1.7 (p.654, where E4's quoted display is). Statuses: this is the best-grounded library list I have reviewed — all 28 declarations behind the 14 library items resolve at the pins, from CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma and UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion through Int.Matrix.exists_ne_zero_int_vec_norm_le, MeromorphicOn.circleAverage_log_norm, Chebyshev.psi_ge, Subgroup.goursat and groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact to ValueDistribution.proximity and Tau Ceti's UpperHalfPlane.discCoordinateEquiv. All eleven findings are confirmed, each read at its locator in the decrypted published text and checked: E1's printed H¹(Γ(5), F₃)^{SL₂(F₅)} = 0 is false because SL₂(F₅) is perfect and H¹(SL₂(Z), F₃) = F₃ restricts injectively; E4's factor is inverted (right multiplication by diag(p, 1/p) gives (ap, b/p²; cp², d/p)); E6's counterexample works with E = ⟨−I⟩ as fixed on p.653, so the printed kernel is ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩ ∩ Γ(p) and not Γ(Np); E7 is a real gap, since §4.3 uses G_{2N} ⊂ ⟨E, Γ(2N)⟩ and the construction on p.656 only gives level dividing 2N; E10 recomputes — with (2/π)K(16x) = Σ C(2n,n)²xⁿ the corrected identity gives −4, −12, −80 at n = 1, 2, 3 against 4/(1−2n), and the printed form is its negative, as its value at x = 0 already shows; and E11 is a genuine hole, the case p = ℓ = 2 of Lemma 4.5.6's n = 1 claim, repaired by SL₂(Z₂)^{ab} ≅ Z/4. Nothing was corrected, rejected or deleted, and I add no finding: I read the published text around each finding and the statements the routes cite, not all 76 pages line by line.
